admission.justification: A future classifier must not merge two path-keyed obligations into a guessed renamed item and lose deletion/addition attribution.

alternatives.option: Represent a source rename as deletion of its old path and addition of its new path in the path-keyed changed-file inventory.
alternatives.reason: Appendix151 states this identity choice explicitly. The lane consumes the shared measurement and projects its concrete path, including the absent side for added/deleted changes, rather than inventing cross-path identity.

alternatives.option: Collapse the two changed-file items into a rename identity inferred across paths.
alternatives.reason: Every item is keyed by path; collapsing the paths would change item identity and could discard an independently relevant old/new attribution answer.
alternatives.reconsider_when: An approved requirement deliberately changes changed-item identity and specifies how both path obligations and historical linkage survive.

consequences: A future classifier must not merge two path-keyed obligations into a guessed renamed item and lose deletion/addition attribution.
No prohibition on Git itself detecting renames for other purposes and no claim that this projection owns the underlying Git measurement.
context: Approved MIK-R57@v2 appendix83/151 and rule6 require this by-design choice to be recorded, not deferred as a gap. Source obligation: MIK-R57@v2 by-design rename. This is the requirement-prescribed boundary, not a claim that an undocumented alternative was seriously weighed.
decider: Approved MIK-R57@v2 under D18/D47/D48; Curator records the specified boundary under constrains_future_work.
